questions.question: The Vedangas are Hindu auxiliary disciplines that originated in ancient times and are linked to the study of the Vedas. These are _______ in number.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vedangas are six auxiliary disciplines associated with the study of the Vedas.
 
• They were developed in ancient India to support the proper understanding and interpretation of the Vedas.
 
• The six Vedangas are: Shiksha (Phonetics), Vyakarana (Grammar), Chandas (Meter), Nirukta (Etymology), Jyotisha (Astronomy), and Kalpa (Rituals).
 
• Each Vedanga serves a specific purpose in ensuring the accurate preservation, recitation, and understanding of the Vedic texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiksha (Phonetics)**

 
 
• Shiksha deals with the sounds of the Sanskrit language, including the rules of pronunciation, accent, and intonation.
 
• It is essential for maintaining the oral tradition of the Vedas by ensuring accurate and consistent recitation.
 
 
 
• **Vyakarana (Grammar)**
 
 
• Vyakarana is the study of Sanskrit grammar and linguistic analysis.
 
• The most famous text of Vyakarana is Panini's Ashtadhyayi, which codifies the rules of Sanskrit grammar.
 
 
 
• **Chandas (**M**etrics****)**
 
 
• Chandas is the study of poetic meters used in Vedic texts.
 
• It helps in understanding the structure and rhythmic patterns of Vedic hymns.
 
 
 
• **Nirukta (Etymology)**
 
 
• Nirukta involves the interpretation and explanation of difficult Vedic words.
 
• Yaska's Nirukta is a significant work in this field, providing meanings and contexts of Vedic terms.

• The plan focused heavily on agriculture, irrigation, and energy to boost the economy.

• **Five-Year Plans**

questions.question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?

options.text: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indirect transmission refers to the transfer of infectious agents to a susceptible person through a contaminated intermediate object or organism.
 
• The five Fs of indirect transmission are: **Flies, fingers, fomites, food, and fluid**.
 
• These five Fs represent the common pathways through which pathogens can be transmitted indirectly.
 
• Understanding these pathways is crucial in implementing effective infection control measures to prevent the spread of diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flies**: Flies can act as vectors by carrying pathogens on their bodies and contaminating food or surfaces they land on.
 
• **Fingers**: Hands can become contaminated through contact with infected surfaces, body fluids, or during the handling of contaminated objects, leading to the spread of pathogens.
 
• **Fomites**: Fomites are inanimate objects like doorknobs, utensils, or clothing that can harbor infectious agents and facilitate their transmission when touched by individuals.
 
• **Food**: Contaminated food can be a source of infection if it is prepared, handled, or stored improperly, allowing pathogens to multiply and cause illness.
 
• **Fluid**: Contaminated water or other fluids can serve as a medium for the transmission of pathogens, especially in areas with poor sanitation and hygiene practices.

questions.question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor is the head of a state in India.
 
• The Governor's role includes giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the legislative assembly of a state with the prior permission of the Governor.
 
• The Governor has the authority to recommend the introduction of money bills in the state legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill**

 
 
• A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It deals with issues related to taxation, borrowing of money by the government, expenditure from the state or central consolidated fund, and other financial matters.
 
• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (at the central level) or the Legislative Assembly (at the state level).
 
• The Rajya Sabha (at the central level) or the Legislative Council (at the state level) can only make recommendations on a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly may choose to accept or reject.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor**
 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• The Governor acts as a representative of the President in the state.
 
• In addition to legislative duties, the Governor has executive and judicial functions.
 
• The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense.
 
 
 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**
 
 
• The CAG is an authority established by the Constitution of India under Article 148.
 
• The CAG audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and the state governments, including those of bodies and authorities substantially financed by the government.
 
• The CAG reports are laid before the Parliament and state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Finance Minister**
 
 
• The Finance Minister is a key position in the government responsible for managing the financial resources of the country or state.
 
• The Finance Minister presents the annual budget, oversees revenue collection, and manages public expenditure.
 
• The Finance Minister plays a crucial role in economic planning and development.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the gap between male and female literacy rate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1668**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, the literacy rate among males was **82.14%** and among females was **65.46%**.
 
• The gap between male and female literacy rates is calculated as the difference between these two percentages.
 
• The literacy rate gap is thus **82.14% - 65.46% = 16.68%**.
 
• This percentage gap is equivalent to **0.1668 when expressed as a decimal**, which is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is the procedure of systematically acquiring and recording information about the members of a given population.
 
• It is a regularly occurring and official count of a particular population.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted once every ten years.
 
• The first complete census in India was conducted in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who can read and write with understanding in a given population.
 
• It is an important indicator of the educational level of a population.
 
• High literacy rates are often associated with higher levels of economic development.
 
 
 
• **Gender Disparity in Literacy**
 
 
• Gender disparity in literacy refers to the difference in literacy rates between males and females.
 
• This disparity is often a result of socio-cultural factors that prioritize male education over female education.
 
• Reducing this gap is crucial for achieving gender equality and empowering women.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chittaranjan Das was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and political leader known as 'Deshbandhu', which means 'Friend of the Nation'.
 
• He played a significant role in the Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was the founder of the Swaraj Party along with Motilal Nehru, which aimed at attaining self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• He was also a renowned lawyer and defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case, further establishing his reputation as a key figure in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, it was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement aimed at resisting British rule through nonviolent means.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation across India with actions like boycotting British goods, institutions, and services.
 
• Chittaranjan Das played a crucial role in galvanizing support for the movement, especially in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj Party**
 
 
• Founded by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru in 1923, the Swaraj Party aimed to achieve self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• The party sought to enter legislative councils through elections to obstruct and eventually end British rule from within the system.
 
• This was a strategic shift from Gandhi's non-cooperation approach and aimed at more direct political engagement.
 
 
 
• **Alipore Bomb Case**
 
 
• In 1908, Aurobindo Ghosh and several others were arrested for their alleged involvement in a conspiracy to bomb a British magistrate's carriage.
 
• Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo Ghosh, and his eloquent defense played a significant role in the acquittal of Ghosh.
 
• This case was a landmark in the Indian legal history and highlighted the role of Indian lawyers in the freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• Established in 1885, the Indian National Congress (INC) was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was an active member of the INC and held significant positions, including the President of the Gaya session in 1922.
 
• His contributions to the INC were vital in shaping the strategies and policies of the freedom struggle during the early 20th century.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizens?

options.text: To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• These duties are specified in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are a set of 11 duties that are expected to be performed by the citizens of India.
 
• Mandatory national service of 5 years is not included among these Fundamental Duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are moral obligations that are intended to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among the citizens of India.
 
• These duties are modeled on the Soviet Constitution and are aimed at upholding the spirit of patriotism and unity.
 
• Some of the key Fundamental Duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and safeguarding public property.
 
• Though not enforceable by law, these duties serve as a constant reminder to the citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• This amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" because it brought about wide-ranging changes to the Constitution.
 
• It introduced the Fundamental Duties and made several other significant changes, including the addition of the words "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble.

questions.question: A person borrowed some money on simple interest. After 4 years, he returned (9)/(5) of the money to lender. What was the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Principal be 5 units.

Amount returned = 9 units ⇒ Total Interest = 9 − 5 = 4 units.

Interest for 4 years = 4 units ⇒ Interest for 1 year = 1 unit.

Rate of Interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100.

Rate = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20% p.a.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 9/5 of Principal (P)

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = P + SI

 
 Principal = 5 units
 
 
 Interest = 4 units

 

 Total Amount Returned = 9 units

 Time (T) = 4 Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Principal (P) = x

⇒ Amount (A) = 9x/5

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = A − P = 9x/5 − x = 4x/5

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 4x/5 = (x × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = 4R ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = R ÷ 25

⇒ R = (4 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated uniformly on the original principal throughout the loan period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total money paid back to the lender is called the Amount. Formula: Amount = Principal + Simple Interest.

Effective Rate of Interest

In Simple Interest, the effective rate for 'T' years is simply (R × T)%. For example, 20% p.a. for 4 years means the total interest generated is 80% of the Principal.
</p

questions.question: Every month, a man consumes 20 kg of rice and 8 kg of wheat. The price of rice is 20% of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of ₹300 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by 20%, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of ₹300? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price ratio of Rice to Wheat = 20% = 1 : 5.

Expenditure ratio (Rice : Wheat) = (20 × 1) : (8 × 5) = 20 : 40 = 1 : 2.

Wheat expenditure increases by 20%, so extra cost = 20% of 2 units = 0.4 units.

To keep total expenditure constant, rice expenditure must decrease by 0.4 units.

Since rice price is constant, % reduction in consumption = (0.4 ÷ 1) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total expenditure = ₹300

Initial consumption of rice (Cᵣ) = 20 kg

Initial consumption of wheat (Cw) = 8 kg

Price of rice (Pᵣ) = 20% of Price of wheat (Pw) ⇒ Pw = 5 × Pᵣ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b2dce248bf23b0465e3954c1af064ed3c6e8e9d7896de5f01d9282c3d837f39.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total expenditure = (Cᵣ × Pᵣ) + (Cw × Pw) = 300

⇒ (20 × Pᵣ) + (8 × 5 Pᵣ) = 300

⇒ 20 Pᵣ + 40 Pᵣ = 300

⇒ 60 Pᵣ = 300 ⇒ Pᵣ = ₹5/kg

⇒ Pw = 5 × 5 = ₹25/kg

Initial expenditures:

⇒ Wheat expenditure = 8 × 25 = ₹200

⇒ Rice expenditure = 20 × 5 = ₹100

New conditions:

⇒ Price of wheat increases by 20%

⇒ New price of wheat = 25 × 1.20 = ₹30/kg

⇒ New wheat expenditure = 8 × 30 = ₹240

⇒ New rice expenditure = 300 − 240 = ₹60 (Since total is constant at ₹300)

⇒ New rice consumption = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 kg (Since Pᵣ is constant at ₹5/kg)

Percentage reduction in rice consumption:

⇒ Reduction = 20 − 12 = 8 kg

⇒ Percentage reduction = (8 ÷ 20) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Expenditure Formula

Total Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure is constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional.

Percentage Increase / Decrease

Percentage Change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. It is always calculated on the base or original value.

Constant Total Expenditure with Multiple Items

If Total Expenditure = Exp₁ + Exp₂ is constant, any absolute increase in Exp₁ must be exactly balanced by an equal absolute decrease in Exp₂.

questions.question: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time traveled is constant, the ratio of distances covered is directly equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of distances (Policeman : Thief) = Ratio of speeds = 5 : 4

Difference in distance ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

This 1 unit difference corresponds to the initial gap of 150 m.

Distance covered by the thief = 4 units = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between the policeman and the thief = 150 m

Ratio of speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 5 : 4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f7c426194eb344902d1d5298451d3b3e2043f5b259ee938cc1b85a3bc9c3f17.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the policeman be 5x m/s and the thief be 4x m/s.

⇒ Relative speed = 5x − 4x = x m/s

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = Initial Distance Gap ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Catching Time = 150 ÷ x seconds

⇒ Distance covered by the thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Catching Time

⇒ Distance = 4x × (150 ÷ x)

⇒ Distance = 4 × 150 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Constant Time Property

If two moving bodies travel for exactly the same amount of time, the distance covered by each is directly proportional to their respective speeds (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).
</p

1 / (1 + cos θ) + 1 / (1 − cos θ)

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

questions.question:
Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 48 minutes and 66 minutes, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously,

then after how many minutes should pipe B be closed so that the tank gets filled in 32 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of tank = LCM of 48 and 66 = 528 units.

Efficiency of A = 528 ÷ 48 = 11 units/min, Efficiency of B = 528 ÷ 66 = 8 units/min.

Since the tank fills in 32 minutes, Pipe A operates for all 32 minutes.

Work done by Pipe A alone = 32 × 11 = 352 units.

Remaining work done by Pipe B = 528 − 352 = 176 units.

Time Pipe B was kept open = 176 ÷ 8 = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 48 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B = 66 minutes

Total time required to fill the tank = 32 minutes

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank (Total Work) = LCM of 48 and 66 = 528 units

⇒ Pipe B is closed early, meaning Pipe A runs for the entire duration of 32 minutes.

⇒ Work done by Pipe A in 32 minutes = 32 × 11 = 352 units

⇒ Remaining work to be completed by Pipe B = 528 − 352 = 176 units

⇒ Time for which Pipe B was kept open = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time for Pipe B = 176 ÷ 8 = 22 minutes

If Pipe A fills a tank in x hours and Pipe B fills it in y hours, they together will fill it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

questions.question: If 7 tan θ = 3, then (7 sin θ + 5 cos θ) / (7 sin θ - 2 cos θ) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, 7 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3 / 7

Since tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, we can directly substitute sin θ = 3 and cos θ = 7 in the homogeneous expression.

⇒ (7 × 3 + 5 × 7) / (7 × 3 − 2 × 7)

⇒ (21 + 35) / (21 − 14)

⇒ 56 / 7 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

7 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3 / 7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/382583cdf62de3bb4c138e15fba760098371d96045643ab0e26701eb9d71affb.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

Hypotenuse = √(Perpendicular² + Base²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Perpendicular = 3 and Base = 7.

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(3² + 7²) = √(9 + 49) = √58

⇒ sin θ = 3 / √58

⇒ cos θ = 7 / √58

Now, substituting the values into (7 sin θ + 5 cos θ) / (7 sin θ − 2 cos θ):

⇒ [7 × (3 / √58) + 5 × (7 / √58)] / [7 × (3 / √58) − 2 × (7 / √58)]

⇒ [(21 + 35) / √58] / [(21 − 14) / √58]

⇒ (56 / √58) / (7 / √58)

⇒ 56 / 7 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

The primary trigonometric ratios in a right-angled triangle are sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular / Base.

Pythagorean Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

Fundamental Identities

The foundational trigonometric identities are sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: In triangle ABC, the length of side BC is 2 cm less than twice the length of side AB. The length of side AC exceeds the length of side AB by 10 cm. The perimeter of the triangle is 40 cm. Determine the length (in cm) of the smallest side of the triangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the length of the side AB be x cm.

From the given problem, BC = 2x − 2 and AC = x + 10.

Perimeter = AB + BC + AC ⇒ x + 2x − 2 + x + 10 = 40

⇒ 4x + 8 = 40 ⇒ 4x = 32 ⇒ x = 8 cm.

The sides of the triangle are 8 cm, 14 cm, and 18 cm. The smallest side is clearly 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of side BC is 2 cm less than twice the length of side AB.

Length of side AC is 10 cm more than side AB.

Perimeter of triangle = 40 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4582980ffd39d958b96cee6a328efa736c73b57be1ef16fa61c1344ddbee948a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a triangle = Sum of all its three sides (AB + BC + AC)

**Calculations:**

Let the length of side AB be x cm.

⇒ BC = (2x − 2) cm

⇒ AC = (x + 10) cm

⇒ Perimeter = AB + BC + AC

⇒ x + (2x − 2) + (x + 10) = 40

⇒ 4x + 8 = 40

⇒ 4x = 32

⇒ x = 32 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 8 cm

Now, substitute the value of x to find the lengths of the remaining sides:

⇒ AB = 8 cm

⇒ BC = 2 × (8) − 2 = 16 − 2 = 14 cm

⇒ AC = 8 + 10 = 18 cm

Comparing all three sides (8 cm, 14 cm, and 18 cm), the length of the smallest side is AB which equals 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the length of the remaining third side (a + b > c).

Types of Triangles by Sides

Triangles are classified by their sides as Scalene (all 3 sides unequal), Isosceles (any 2 sides equal), and Equilateral (all 3 sides equal).

Perimeter and Semi-perimeter

The perimeter is simply the total outer boundary sum (a + b + c), while the semi-perimeter (s) used in finding area via Heron's formula is (a + b + c) ÷ 2.
</p

questions.question: If cot⁴Φ − cot²Φ = 1, then the value of cos⁴Φ + cos²Φ is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: cot⁴Φ − cot²Φ = 1

⇒ cot⁴Φ = 1 + cot²Φ = cosec²Φ

⇒ cos⁴Φ / sin⁴Φ = 1 / sin²Φ ⇒ cos⁴Φ = sin²Φ

⇒ cos⁴Φ = 1 − cos²Φ ⇒ cos⁴Φ + cos²Φ = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cot⁴Φ − cot²Φ = 1

**Formula Used:**

cosec²Φ − cot²Φ = 1

sin²Φ + cos²Φ = 1

cotΦ = cosΦ / sinΦ

cosecΦ = 1 / sinΦ

**Calculations:**

⇒ cot⁴Φ − cot²Φ = 1

⇒ cot⁴Φ = 1 + cot²Φ

Using the identity cosec²Φ − cot²Φ = 1,

⇒ cot⁴Φ = cosec²Φ

Converting cotΦ and cosecΦ to their basic sine and cosine forms,

⇒ (cos⁴Φ / sin⁴Φ) = (1 / sin²Φ)

Multiplying both sides by sin⁴Φ,

⇒ cos⁴Φ = sin⁴Φ / sin²Φ

⇒ cos⁴Φ = sin²Φ

Using the fundamental identity sin²Φ = 1 − cos²Φ,

⇒ cos⁴Φ = 1 − cos²Φ

Transposing cos²Φ to the left-hand side,

⇒ cos⁴Φ + cos²Φ = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Quotient Identities

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ and cotθ = cosθ / sinθ.

Reciprocal Identities

sinθ × cosecθ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1, and tanθ × cotθ = 1.
</p

questions.question:
For the following equations, what are the values of a and b to have infinitely many solutions?

ax + by = 2

3x - (5 - 2a)y = 6
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For infinitely many solutions, the two equations must be identical when their constant terms are matched.

Multiply the first equation by 3 to match the constant 6 in the second equation:

⇒ 3ax + 3by = 6

Compare coefficients directly with the second equation 3x − (5 − 2a)y = 6:

⇒ 3a = 3 ⇒ a = 1 | 3b = −(5 − 2a) ⇒ 3b = −(5 − 2) ⇒ b = −1

**∴ The correct answer is a = 1, b = −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: ax + by = 2

Equation 2: 3x − (5 − 2a)y = 6

**Formula Used:**

For two linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ to have infinitely many solutions, their corresponding coefficients must be proportional:

a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Here, a₁ = a, b₁ = b, c₁ = 2

⇒ And, a₂ = 3, b₂ = −(5 − 2a), c₂ = 6

⇒ Applying the condition for infinite solutions: a / 3 = b / −(5 − 2a) = 2 / 6

⇒ Simplify the constant ratio: 2 / 6 = 1 / 3

⇒ Equating the x coefficients to the constant ratio: a / 3 = 1 / 3

⇒ a = 1

⇒ Equating the y coefficients to the constant ratio: b / −(5 − 2a) = 1 / 3

⇒ Substitute the value of a = 1 into the equation: b / −(5 − 2 × 1) = 1 / 3

⇒ b / −(5 − 2) = 1 / 3

⇒ b / −3 = 1 / 3

⇒ 3b = −3

⇒ b = −1

**∴ The correct answer is a = 1, b = −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unique Solution

A system of equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect at exactly one point. The mathematical condition is a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂.

No Solution

A system of equations has no solution if the lines are strictly parallel and never intersect. The condition is a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂.

Infinitely Many Solutions

A system of equations has infinitely many solutions if the two lines are coincident (overlapping each other entirely). The condition is a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂.
</p

questions.question: Which of following numbers is NOT divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 11 rule: Difference between sums of alternating digits must be a multiple of 11.

Checking 128041 directly:

Sum of alternating digits (odd positions) = 1 + 0 + 2 = 3

Sum of alternating digits (even positions) = 4 + 8 + 1 = 13

Difference = 13 − 3 = 10 (Not a multiple of 11).

**∴ The correct answer is 128041.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four numbers: 109153, 5445, 128041, and 80124.

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd positions and the sum of its digits at even positions is exactly divisible by 11 (i.e., 0, 11, 22, etc.).

**Calculation:**

⇒ For 109153: Sum of odd place digits = 3 + 1 + 0 = 4; Sum of even place digits = 5 + 9 + 1 = 15.

⇒ Difference = 15 − 4 = 11 (Divisible by 11).

Let m = 16 and n = 8.

Substitute these values in the expression: (m − 16)³ + (n − 8)³

⇒ (16 − 16)³ + (8 − 8)³ = 0 + 0 = 0

m + n = 24

Let a = m − 16 and b = n − 8

⇒ a + b = (m − 16) + (n − 8)

⇒ a + b = m + n − 24

Substitute the value of m + n = 24:

⇒ a + b = 24 − 24

⇒ a + b = 0

Since a + b = 0, we can say that a³ + b³ = 0.

⇒ (m − 16)³ + (n − 8)³ = 0

questions.question: The ratio between male and female members in a club is 2 : 3. If the number of male members is increased by 200, the ratio becomes 5 : 6. How many female members are there in the club?

questions.question: In a garden, there are 6 daisy plants the first year. Each year, a gardener adds 3 new daisy plants. He has 26 jasmine plants the first year and loses 2 each year. When will the number of daisy plants equal to the number of jasmine plants after the first year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial difference between jasmine and daisy plants = 26 − 6 = 20

Relative change per year = Daisy (+3) − Jasmine (−2) = 5 plants per year

Years required to become equal = Initial Difference ÷ Relative Change

⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of daisy plants (First year) = 6

Number of daisy plants added per year = 3

Initial number of jasmine plants (First year) = 26

Number of jasmine plants lost per year = 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/099914ac0b658f65f723599dd7d6968cf012e82d4317403f40e6dcd9d21f6aae.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total plants after n years = Initial quantity + (Rate of change × n)

**Calculations:**

Let the required number of years after the first year be n.

⇒ Number of daisy plants after n years = 6 + 3n

⇒ Number of jasmine plants after n years = 26 − 2n

According to the question, both quantities become equal:

⇒ 6 + 3n = 26 − 2n

⇒ 3n + 2n = 26 − 6

⇒ 5n = 20

⇒ n = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

This problem uses the concept of an Arithmetic Progression where a constant value is added or subtracted every interval. The nth term of an AP is given by Tₙ = a + (n−1)d, but since we are looking at 'n' years *after* the first year, it functions as Tₙ = a + nd.

Relative Speed Concept

Similar to relative speed in distance problems, when two opposing quantities move towards each other, their progression rates are added together. Here, one quantity increases by 3 and the other decreases by 2, making the effective catch-up rate 3 + 2 = 5 units per year.

Linear Equations in One Variable

Setting two linear expressions equal to each other helps algebraically to find their intersection point, representing the exact time when both dependent variables yield the same total value.
</p
